paragraphs.speaker: Host (Aldo Arzapalo)
paragraphs.text: Hello, good night, welcome everyone, in person and online. We are very happy for this first anniversary celebration. And we're in a gala, it’s amazing, because we have special and important guest — Tim Lowenhaupt. He comes from Rimrock. He has been practicing for around 16 years and he has done three one-month silent retreats. He's a great meditator, a great practitioner, and the director of V Houses. And we're very honored to have him here tonight. Tonight's talk is about The Eye of Courage: Blindspots and Leadership. Thank you, everyone, for being here, and we're going to start.

chapters.title: Why I almost taught in Spanish

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I might speak Spanish sometimes, so then you'll need to translate into English. Right now we have about 80 people online, and we're translating it into five or six languages live. So part of this is a welcome to the rest of the V Houses world of what's happening here in Mexico. Many people know that we’ve had events here since 2012, I believe, for ACI/V Houses. And this part of the world is unknown to a lot of our students — meaning that in the Americas, there aren't as many students as there are in Europe and Asia. And one of the things I've been thinking a lot about is: how can we activate the Americas as well?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And I had told Rivas, I said, I'm going to try to teach in Spanish. And then I decided — and actually, it's relevant to tonight's talk — I was like, wow, wouldn't it be really cool if we just offered this to everyone? Which gets me out of speaking Spanish. And the second reason I wanted to speak Spanish only is because there are some people here who don't know Spanish yet, and who are getting work permission in Mexico very soon. So I thought it would be really annoying to speak Spanish and then they wouldn't be able to understand.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But part of the creative idea to offer this to the rest of the world was also based in a little bit of fear of teaching in Spanish. I was so excited when the idea came up — like, oh yeah, we'll just offer this to everyone. And then I realized that the creativity was motivated by a fear. The cool idea was then wrapped in this limitation: oh, Tim is not good enough at Spanish to teach a Dharma class, to teach a V Houses class. So thank you, everyone joining online. So then I was thinking, whoa, there has to be something in that that could be useful for teaching. Because I like to teach from a direct experience.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then I was thinking about this beautiful center here — how can we activate? And I use this word "activate": how can we activate in such a way that we have an entire hemisphere of the Americas, and people, that we can reach? I know a lot of new faces here, which is great. And I know a lot of you have a bigger vision — a bigger vision for your own life, and a bigger vision for the people that we can reach.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then I always ask the question: well, why aren't we doing it yet? In parentheses, we probably already are. We're already planting the seeds, we're already germinating some of those seeds. But I want to activate that.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So we're doing this really cool thing in October. And it's a worldwide event that somehow exploded to almost 5,000 people participating online. And not just 5,000 people participating online — the requirement for this event is that people have to do it in person. No, we're not renting a stadium, like a soccer, a football stadium. We've created 280 branch locations around the world.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: Hemos creado 280 sedes alrededor del mundo.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: “Sedes,” right? I learned a new word tonight.
{interpreter laughs}

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So everybody is organizing in person, and then they're going to be receiving the transmission from the land of Rimrock in the United States. And Rimrock is a thriving town of about 2,000 people. Maybe 2,000. In English, we say "the sticks." And we have a beautiful property there that we're going to be transmitting from. It's in northern Arizona.

chapters.title: How the center began — Rivas's pitch

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I remember about two years ago, Rivas came to me at Rob Haggerty's house in Rimrock. And as is normal with a group of Mexicans, they were having a party. Loud music, everybody's dancing. Oh my God, I can't believe these people, they're having so much fun. And I'm grumpy. It's so irritating to be grumpy when everyone else is having fun. And Rivas comes up to me, and he saw that I was grumpy. He's like, Tim, I have a great idea — this is the perfect time to pitch a new idea. Tim's a little grumpy, he's tired. I wanted to hang with all my Mexican friends, but I didn't want that, exactly.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And he said, Tim, we need a center in Guadalajara. We need a place where we can bring people together to teach these phenomenal ideas. And I'll tell you, as director of V Houses for 10 years, what I thought about it. I was like, can you just go to a yoga studio three nights a week, grow a community first, like three times a week, and then start a center? Because my mind works in business, like step-by-step business. And sometimes I forget about seeds. We all do. We think we know better. We think we know more. We think we know what the right thing to do is, because that's how it's supposed to be done.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And he made a really good pitch. I still was grumpy. I love these guys. We've been friends for many, many years. And I do have a grumpy side. We've got to find a better word for this.

chapters.title: Needing friends, and hitting the wall

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But you know, Gina said something really cool to me many years ago. I'm kind of very independent. So I get grumpy when I have to do something where my independence is threatened. And again, limiting beliefs — we're going to talk about this.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Ten years ago, in the V Houses we have a series of teachings where, when you arrive at a certain level, you're admitted into the advanced teachings. And I wanted to do them by myself. I didn't want people to know that I was studying. I just wanted that one-on-one relationship with the teacher, like everybody wants. I wanted it to be private. And instead of that, my teacher joyfully invited me to join a group of Mexican friends, and we all started those advanced teachings together.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And one day I was sitting with Gina, and I was in one of my grumpy moods. I don't know what was going on, but she said something really cool to me. She got me to question why it was that my teacher invited me to join with all the Mexican friends. And she said, it's because you don't have friends, Tim. I have very few friends. I needed my group of homies. I needed that group of people. Being alone was not working for me. My grand independence, that I can do everything by myself — my teacher was like, nope, you're going to go hang out with these people.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And we've developed beautiful friendships over the years. But I hit the wall of the limit of that independence about two years ago. And my whole body crashed — mentally, physically, emotionally. And it was a process of rebuilding.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So going back to Rivas — he had so much passion in his presentation to start this center that I was like, let's let go of the way you think things should be, Tim. And I said to myself, let's leave the idea of how you think things should be, and let's trust in something different. And we went to our mutual boss. And I said, let's try it. And I put together a plan on how we were going to try to fundraise. And we're going to talk about that later. Because this center is due to the kindness of many, many people here in Mexico, and also on the other side of the Pacific Ocean. We all believed in something. There was a vision.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So we're here on the first anniversary. We have a nearly full room. And we invited the rest of the world to watch as we're celebrating our first year.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So I was thinking for quite a while, like, what could I offer coming down here — not just to celebrate, but is there something we can work together on that helps grow the center, but also activate the Americas? Because yes, we do want to build a thriving community here, and continue to build that community here in Guadalajara. But let's take a 30,000-foot view — a 30,000-feet view from an airplane — and look down and see what else we can do.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then I thought about a lot of my friends here, and how we've grown over the last 10, 15 years. And recently the meditations and the teachings we've been given are kind of pushing us to grow, pushing us to go further. And I just was like, let's keep building, let's keep growing. Let's celebrate the incredible things that were done in this center the last year. And what seeds can we put into place to activate not only this local community, but spread these ideas much beyond this community?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now, I have a proposal. We spend so much time on: what seeds do I need to plant? What four-step plan do I need to put into place? A lot of us arrive at a time in our practice when we've been planting seeds for so long, but we're not seeing the results yet. And oftentimes I see it in so many people. I travel around the world constantly.
